title: Vessel Condition Survey Dubai | Drydocks World & Jebel Ali
description: Vessel condition surveys in Dubai at Drydocks World, Jebel Ali or the anchorages: structure, coatings, thickness and machinery for Gulf owners and lenders.
h1: Condition surveys for Gulf owners and managers in Dubai: in dock, alongside or at anchor
intro: Dubai is where many owners, ship managers and charterers trading in the Gulf and the wider Indian Ocean decide which ships to keep trading, charter out, refinance or send to dock. A vessel condition survey gives those decisions a measured basis: structure, tanks, coatings and running machinery rated area by area, with every defect ranked for action. It can be carried out while a ship lies at Drydocks World, during a longer call at Jebel Ali, at the Dubai anchorages or at the smaller yards of Dubai Maritime City. For each job the team flies in from India, with UAE visas processed before departure.

highlights.h: Weeks ahead of the Drydocks World slot
highlights.p: A condition survey at the anchorage or alongside, some weeks before a booked docking at Port Rashid, tells the superintendent which tanks, pipes and closing appliances need work. The repair specification then goes to the yard complete, rather than growing once the ship is in dock and staging is rigged.

highlights.h: Gulf service written into the findings
highlights.p: Warm, highly saline seawater and humid nights wear coatings and steel faster than temperate trades. Surveys of ships that have spent years in the Gulf look hardest at the upper parts of ballast tanks, void spaces, under-deck structure and scrubber piping, where that environment shows first.

Supply vessels and anchor-handling tugs in Dubai move between operators' contracts. An owner's survey before a new charter starts, or after one ends, records the cargo deck, stern area, tanks and machinery in measured terms, so the vessel's condition at each handover is on file.

sections.h: Where in Dubai can a vessel condition survey be carried out?
p: Drydocks World at Port Rashid offers the fullest access. A tanker, gas carrier, bulk carrier or offshore unit there lies in dock or at a repair berth with staging, lighting and gas-free certificates arranged by the yard for its own work, and the survey is slotted into that sequence through the owner's site team. The bottom shell, sea chests, rudder and propeller area are dry and can be included, and the yard's project manager hears about any additional work while the ship is still on the blocks.

Elsewhere the survey follows the ship's window. At the Dubai anchorages, tankers and bulk carriers waiting for a berth, orders or a docking slot can open ballast tanks and, in ballast, holds, with the team arriving by launch through the agent. At Jebel Ali, ro-ro, multipurpose and break-bulk ships sometimes stay long enough for a meaningful survey, while mainline container ships allow only deck, coamings, engine room and accessible piping. The smaller repair facilities of Dubai Maritime City take tugs, workboats and offshore support vessels, where tanks and machinery are freely accessible during a repair period.
list: Drydocks World, Port Rashid: complete condition surveys in dock or at the repair berths, including the external hull
Dubai anchorages: ballast tanks, holds in ballast, deck, closing appliances and machinery on ships waiting for berths or orders
Jebel Ali Port: deck, coamings, hatch covers, engine room and accessible tanks on ro-ro, multipurpose and container ships
Dubai Maritime City yards: cargo deck, stern area, tanks and machinery on offshore support vessels, tugs and workboats
Mina Rashid cruise terminal: machinery spaces and accessible piping on cruise ships during winter-season turnarounds

sections.h: Who commissions condition surveys in Dubai, and for what purpose?
p: Technical managers of Gulf-based fleets are the core of the work. Many run older crude and product tankers and bulk carriers on regional trades, and they use condition surveys to decide what each ship needs before its next renewal survey or docking, and whether a tanker past fifteen years should be prepared for a CAP rating that charterers will read. A survey of each ship in a fleet at the same depth, year after year, turns those decisions from impressions into comparisons.

Charterers and owners use them around handovers. A multipurpose or ro-ro ship redelivered at Jebel Ali at the end of a period, or an offshore vessel returning from a field contract, is surveyed so that the owner holds a measured record of decks, holds, tank tops and machinery at that moment. The charter's own on-hire and off-hire surveyors still attend for the parties, and the P&I club or hull insurer still appoints its own surveyor where it wants one; the owner's survey is in addition to them.

Banks and lessors financing Gulf tonnage form the third group. A periodic condition report, or one at a refinancing, tells the lender in plain terms how structure, coatings and machinery stand and what the next class survey is likely to demand, without valuing the ship.

sections.h: How is a Dubai condition survey planned around heat, humidity and the yard sequence?
p: Temperature governs the working day from late spring to early autumn. Outdoor work in direct sun is restricted in the UAE during the hottest part of summer days, and tanks under a sun-heated deck become punishing by late morning, so ballast tank and void entries are scheduled for the early hours with ventilation started well beforehand, and deck and closing-appliance work is fitted around the midday break. Each technician's time inside a space is limited by the master's entry permit and the team's own heat-stress rules, which the scope allows for from the start.

In dock, the yard's sequence decides the order. Blasting, staging and steel renewal all compete for the same tanks, so the survey plan is agreed with the yard's project manager and the owner's superintendent before arrival, and spaces are surveyed as they are released. Findings that would add steel, pipe renewal or coating repair go to the superintendent the same day, while the class surveyor is still attending and the staging is still in place.

At anchor or at Jebel Ali, the order is set by priority instead: ballast tanks first, then holds or cargo spaces where accessible, then deck, hatch covers, air pipes and mooring gear, and machinery readings with the chief engineer. Shamal winds can make launch boarding at the anchorages awkward, and boarding may have to wait until the sea moderates.

sections.h: What do condition surveys of Gulf-trading ships in Dubai usually find?
p: Ballast tanks on ships with years of Gulf service usually show coating breakdown concentrated in the upper strakes and under the deckhead, where daytime heat and night-time condensation alternate, and the survey rates each tank in the IACS GOOD, FAIR and POOR terms. Void spaces and cofferdams that rarely receive attention often show more wastage than the tanks beside them. On older tankers, pitting in double-bottom tanks and wasted pipe supports along the cargo deck are common; on bulk carriers, hold frames, brackets and hatch cover seals carry the wear.

Scrubber-fitted ships trading on high-sulphur fuel in a region with no emission control area run their systems continuously, and warm seawater speeds up corrosion in wash-water and overboard lines, so those lines are gauged at bends and near the shell connection on every survey. Offshore support vessels show wear on cargo deck plating, the stern roller area and chain lockers, and corrosion in fuel and drill-water tanks. In hot engine rooms, thermal images of switchboards and starter panels and vibration spectra on cooling-water pumps and fans regularly find faults building towards a failure.

Defects are sorted into three priorities, and the most urgent are reported to the master and the technical manager while the team is still aboard. Where magnetic particle testing confirms a crack, the result is filed as the owner's NDT record rather than offered as a class finding.

sections.h: How does an owner's condition survey in Dubai relate to class, CAS, CAP and port state control?
p: A condition survey has no class or flag standing; it is commissioned for a commercial decision and scoped to suit it. It differs from the IMO Condition Assessment Scheme for older single-hull oil tankers and does not produce a class Condition Assessment Programme rating, though it shows a tanker manager where a CAP survey will find trouble. Nor is it a port state control inspection, but because UAE inspections under the Riyadh MoU often turn on wasted air pipes, ventilator coamings, deck plating and hatch coamings, the survey reports those items in a form that can be repaired before arrival.

Thickness readings in the survey are a structured sample for the owner's planning. Atlantis has not yet received UR Z17 approval from any society and is in the process of obtaining it from DNV, Lloyd's Register and ABS, so these readings are not credited to a class survey; where a renewal survey is near, they give a first estimate of the steel the class gauging will call for.

sections.h: Planning a condition survey in Dubai: what to send
p: Send the vessel, the purpose and the expected place: a Drydocks World docking date, a Jebel Ali berth, an anchorage period or a Dubai Maritime City yard. UAE entry visas for the team are processed before it flies from India, usually into Dubai International, with Al Maktoum International as an alternative near Jebel Ali. Yard access at Drydocks World is arranged through the owner's site team, and ISPS gate passes and launches through the ship's agent. Include earlier condition and thickness reports, the class survey status and any report template a charterer, lender or fleet department requires; for fleets with ships at several UAE ports, a list of expected calls lets us plan a sequence along the coast. Write to info@atlantisndt.com or use the enquiry form.

faqs.q: Can a condition survey be done at Drydocks World while the ship is docked?
faqs.a: Yes, and it is the most complete kind. The survey is slotted into the yard's sequence through the owner's site team, so tanks are surveyed as they are released and the bottom shell, sea chests and stern area while the hull is dry. Anything that should be added to the repair work goes to the superintendent the same day, while staging and the class surveyor are still there.

faqs.q: Is it better to survey before the ship arrives at the yard?
faqs.a: For a docking specification, usually yes. A survey at the Dubai anchorages or alongside some weeks before the docking lets the superintendent send the yard a specification that already includes the steel, pipe and coating work the ship needs. The yard can then plan staging, material and labour from the start, and fewer items are discovered and added once the ship is in dock.

faqs.q: How does summer heat in Dubai change the survey?
faqs.a: It shapes the working day. Tank and void entries are moved to the early morning, ventilation runs well before entry, each technician's time inside is limited, and outdoor deck work is fitted around the hottest hours. The scope is planned with that in mind, and if heat stops a space being completed the report says so rather than guessing at its condition.

faqs.q: Can you survey an offshore vessel or tug at a Dubai Maritime City yard?
faqs.a: Yes. During a repair period these vessels can open tanks and run machinery freely, so the survey covers cargo deck plating, stern roller and towing gear foundations, chain lockers, fuel and drill-water tanks, the generators and propulsion machinery. Owners often time it between contracts, so the condition at the end of one charter and the start of the next is on record.

faqs.q: Can one trip cover ships at several UAE ports?
faqs.a: Often. Owners with ships at Jebel Ali, Port Rashid and other ports along the UAE coast can send us the expected calls, and we plan a sequence so one mobilisation from India covers more than one survey. The same method, rating scale and report layout are used on each ship, which keeps a fleet review consistent.

faqs.q: What does a lender receive from a condition survey in Dubai?
faqs.a: An account of how the ship stands and what threatens its remaining trading years: ratings by area, Priority 1 and 2 defects with photographs, measured machinery readings and the work the coming class survey or docking will probably require. No valuation is given, and class records reach the lender through the owner and the classification society rather than through us.
